description: The public Lac Télé peat-loss GitHub repository contains an R and R Markdown workflow for preparing geospatial forest-loss screening products. The README identifies scripts for spatial layers, annual loss areas, stratified validation points, manual-label summaries, sensitivity analysis, figures and metadata checksums. A separate Zenodo software archive of version 1.0.1 names the same workflow and states the MIT licence; the GitHub LICENSE file also contains MIT terms. The code expects local CongoPeat and Hansen-derived input rasters and writes maps, CSV summaries and validation outputs for the Republic of the Congo study landscape. This is a data-preparation and checking tool for green-blue infrastructure scenario inputs, not a hydrodynamic model or general flood simulator. Site-specific paths, input licences and required manual validation labels are limitations for reuse outside Lac Télé. A reviewer-assessed use is rebuilding peat-loss layers before varying flood-storage assumptions. data-hansen-global-forest-change is a related raw forest-change input. No code or dataset archive was downloaded or executed.
